verdict.tagline: Short puzzles and a killer soundtrack make this free gem shine.
not_for_you_if: you struggle with strict move limits
you dislike sudden difficulty spikes in boss fights

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight the short completion time, zero cost, and standout soundtrack that enhances the experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is free to play and can be completed within a short duration.

citations.review_text:
[b]+ Excellent puzzle design:[/b] Starts off simple enough and the base game levels are doable without much memorization. The Ex levels are a completely different discussion. In some cases, you need good reaction time to match your planning. Other require you to remember longer sequences of movements, all while trying to figure out the solution through trial and error.

[b]+ Price:[/b] I can't believe this is free. I would pay good money for this even after beating it.

[b]+ Narrative:[/b] Simple but captivating plot. Characters have real charm and their dialogue and banter is very engaging.

[b]+ Music:[/b] Great soundtrack by Mittsies. Blends in seamlessly with the gameplay to the point you even forget there is a soundtrack. For that reason, I suggest listening to it separately to appreciate why it was nominated for Best Soundtrack during the 2020 Steam Awards.

[b]+ Length:[/b] Takes 1-2h to complete, including the bonus levels. Short enough to beat in one sitting.

This game was very fun to run through!
I played through 100% of the game on Steam Deck, only problem is the game's launcher (Unity "Graphics Quality" window) does not support controller inputs, which is annoying for maybe 8 seconds, but it's otherwise fine.

The game's story is short, simple, and very silly. The art for the game is very nice as well. It's short, being 100% completable in maybe an hour if you really tried, but for a free game that's not a problem really.

If I had to pick anything to complain about, maybe the secret post-game boss is a little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but it's hard to call unfair. I won't get into specifics since I don't want to spoil anything.

9.75/10, if you haven't given this game a shot, you're missing out!

cohorts.summary: Players enjoy the free access and engaging puzzle mechanics alongside a catchy score, though final boss encounters introduce demanding reflex challenges.

claims.claim: The game features block-pushing and turn-based puzzles where players must carefully manage a limited number of moves.

citations.review_text:
[h1]Helltaker[/h1]
[h3]Short and Repetitive Puzzle Game[/h3]
[h3]Free but not really fun to play[/h3]

Helltaker is a small turn-based puzzle game featuring a cast of archetypal female demon characters. The story is deliberately absurd and straightforward, serving mainly as a bland reason to introduce its indulgent cast rather than to tell a compelling narrative. This doesn't necessarily mean the game is bad. Instead, it remains more like a small creative passion project than a fully-fledged game.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
Like its story, the gameplay is fairly simple and it only consists of moving our character logically and strategically through a series of levels, each with a limited number of moves available to solve its puzzles.  The levels are not particularly difficult, but they do require some time to solve, as you need to carefully plan every move. 

One of the game's main issues is the dialogue sequence that takes place after completing each level. Choosing the wrong dialogue option when speaking to one of the demon girls makes you lose and forces you to replay the entire puzzle from the beginning, which can become unnecessarily slow and frustrating despite the levels being relatively short. This overall gameplay decision significantly disrupts the game's pacing.

The only section that offers a slightly different gameplay experience is the final level, which features a boss fight that relies on timing and quick reflexes.

For a brief period, the previous boss fight served as the game's final level. However, in 2021, the game received a free update that added a new storyline, which feels rather poorly connected to the original narrative, along with a handful of new levels. This new section, titled Examtaker, consists of six levels, and a boss fight, that combines the original limited-movement puzzle concept, with only two unlimited-movement levels, and new laser-pattern obstacles. 

Honestly, the new level design is more frustrating and often feels unfair. The lev…

Amazing project from long time internet resident vanripper. 

The gameplay is basically sokoban and a short visual novel dating sim. Other than that, the puzzles do not require a lot of brain CPU time to complete. But, I was bored so I used guides anyway lmao.

Examtaker is the expansion and takes place a long time after the "Helltaker" passed. More puzzles, a different boss, and a new ending. 

Both endings come with recipes in the game folder.

I can only stress this so much: [b]GRAB A COPY[/b]!
Or, well, give it a try, as it's [b]FREE[/b]!

Helltaker is one of those games that you found through one of two ways. The music or the fanart, and both are equally as amazing, but I will be talking about the music, as that's actually in the game.

Firstly, the music. Mittsies soundtracks compliment the overall pacing of the game wonderfully well, and nowhere is this better displayed in the boss fights of the base game and its additional chapter.
Vitality is just one of those tracks that gets stuck in your head in the [i]best[/i] way possible.

Secondly, the art. Helltaker's developer and publish, Vanripper, has a wonderfully unique art style that is somewhere between more western influence and anime influence. The result is something that is not only wonderfully appealing to the eye, but is unique in its own right. As far as I know, this has been unofficially coined "Vanripper Style" or "Vanripperesque", and it is a wonderful art style.

The gameplay itself is fun, with the movements feeling response, fast and delightfully animated to go along with it, with the puzzles often not being too challenging, but you still have to use your brain with the limited amount of steps you have before the protagonist gets struck by lightning. Literally.
The sound design is punchy with some wonderful effects that match the intensity and speed of your movements and attacks. And with some secrets hidden throughout that actually trigger a whole different ending to the game, what more could you ask for? 

What's more, is if you enjoy the visuals and the aesthetics of the game and the designs of the subsequent horned and well dressed demons you will meet, completing the game will allow you to see the character sheets, along with some of Vanripper's own written commentary in their design and thought processes behind said designs.

[spoiler]Modeus is the best demon Fight me.[/spoiler]
A handful of block-pushing puzzles with each one punctuated by chatting up a cute demon lady in businesswear. It's a little treat.

It's a good puzzle game with a sortof bullet hell level.
And yes, it has good art.

The puzzles are interesting and fun to solve. The boss fights that turn into Bullet Hells make me want to smash a ladle over the fingers of whoever decided that was an ok thing to do. Fantastic game though, loved the music, art style, and overall design. Except the bosses, those made me so angry I woke up my whole house.
